svg.title: Robotics capacity, utilization and cash-flow model
svg.desc: Define a common period and task mix. Estimate capacity and actual output separately. Output utilization is actual output divided by sustainable capacity. Time utilization is productive robot-hours divided by scheduled robot-hours. Net annual cash benefits determine payback in years and cumulative ROI over a stated horizon. No universal economic or congestion threshold is asserted.

g.text: Robotics: capacity to cash flow
Use one task mix, operating schedule and currency throughout.
1. Sustainable capacity and achieved output
Capacity = minimum of fleet and workstation capacity (tasks/hour).
Fleet lower bound = ceil(peak tasks/hour ÷ tasks/robot-hour).
Validate availability, charging, congestion and shared constraints.
2. Utilization is not a capacity-to-demand ratio
Output utilization = completed tasks ÷ sustainable task capacity
over the same period. Example: 600 ÷ 1,000 = 60%.
Time utilization = productive ÷ scheduled robot-hours.
Capacity ÷ demand is a separate ratio, not utilization.
3. Net cash benefits, not gross labor displacement
Sₜ = avoidable labor cash cost + other incremental cash benefits
− incremental operating cash costs (currency per year).
C₀ = initial installed investment. Count every cost only once.
4. Separate time to recovery from return
Simple payback = C₀ ÷ S (years; constant annual S > 0).
Horizon ROI = (Σ Sₜ − C₀) ÷ C₀ (C₀ > 0; t = 1…H).
Example: $300k invested, $100k/year net → 3-year payback;
5-year undiscounted ROI = 66.7%. Example only, not a benchmark.
No universal utilization or congestion threshold is established.
Definitions, assumptions, limitations and references appear in the article.
